sources.title: Korean Education: Educational Thought, Systems and Content
sources.institution: Jeong Mee-Ryang and Lee Woojin; translated by Sohn Tae-soo; The Academy of Korean Studies, Understanding Korea No. 9 (2018)
sources.locator: Printed pp. 30–32, The Civil Service Examination of the Goryeo Dynasty (PDF pages 17–18, one-based); title and publication details on PDF page 3. Extracted text read after an ordinary download of this exact public URL following a web-tool timeout.
sources.asWorded: In 958, King Gwangjong adopted the civil service examination
sources.originalChronology: The book explicitly dates Gwangjong's adoption of the examination to 958. Its discussion of eligibility, examination types and examiner-candidate patronage describes the wider Goryeo system, without assigning every feature to 958.
sources.scopedClaim: The examination recruited government officials and was intended to strengthen royal authority and a centralized bureaucracy. The account recognizes Silla antecedents, restricted eligibility and elite patronage; it does not establish universal access or the immediate displacement of powerful families.

sources.title: History of the Civil Service Examination
sources.institution: Ministry of Personnel Management, Republic of Korea
sources.locator: English text in 1,200-year History of the Civil Service Examination, paragraphs on Silla 788 and Goryeo 958; web lines 149–155. Public institutional overview, not a primary medieval document.
sources.asWorded: In 958, during the reign of King Gwangjong of Goryeo
sources.originalChronology: The English overview explicitly dates the introduction of gwageo under Gwangjong to 958 and separately dates a Silla examination antecedent to 788. No new conversion or reign arithmetic is used.
sources.scopedClaim: Goryeo introduced gwageo for appointment to government posts on Ssanggi's recommendation. The overview's celebratory description of fair and objective examinations is not adopted as evidence of equal access.

date.noteEn: Both institutional accounts date Gwangjong's introduction of the examination system to 958. This dates the reform, not every later examination practice. Silla had an earlier examination tradition; no day or month is assigned.

events.titleEn: Gwangjong introduces civil service examinations in Goryeo
events.summaryEn: Gwangjong introduces examinations to recruit government officials. The reform aims to strengthen royal authority and build a more centralized civil administration; it does not establish equal access to office.
events.selectionNote: A major regional change in recruitment to government service, distinct from Goryeo's foundation in 918 and consolidation in 936. The sources identify a reform aimed at centralizing royal administration; the claim does not date every later rule to 958, imply universal eligibility or declare the immediate elimination of aristocratic influence.
